Merge Neighbourhood Analysis Results

Source: R/merge_nhood_results.R
merge_nhood_results.Rd

Merges any number of neighbourhood analysis dataframes stored in the metadata slot of a neighbourhood object. Automatically detects which dataframes exist, validates neighbourhood consistency across all sources, and handles redundant columns.

Usage

merge_nhood_results(
  object,
  dataframe_names = c("nhood_diversity", "nhood_shm"),
  merge_key = "nhood",
  size_col = "nhood_size",
  verbose = TRUE,
  result_name = "merged_nhood_analysis"
)

Arguments

object

A SingleCellExperiment or Milo object containing neighbourhood analysis results in its metadata slot.

dataframe_names

Character vector of metadata slot names to merge. Defaults to c("nhood_diversity", "nhood_shm"). Must contain at least two names.

merge_key

Column to merge on (default: "nhood").

size_col

Column name containing neighbourhood size information, used to validate that all dataframes describe the same neighbourhoods. Can be a single string (same column name expected in all dataframes) or a named character vector mapping each dataframe name to its size column, e.g. c(nhood_data = "nhood_size", nhood_shm = "n_cells"). Dataframes not present in a named vector fall back to "nhood_size". Set to NULL to skip the size consistency check entirely.

verbose

Print merge details (default: TRUE).

result_name

Name for the merged output in metadata (default: "merged_nhood_analysis").

Value

Updated object with merged dataframe stored in metadata(object)[[result_name]].

Details

Dataframe availability:

  1. Multiple dataframes found — validates shared neighbourhoods then merges all sequentially on merge_key using inner joins, removing redundant columns at each step.

  2. Only one dataframe found — halts with an error (a merge requires at least two inputs)

  3. No dataframes found — halts with an error

  4. Result already exists — overwrites with a warning.

Neighbourhood validation (two-stage):

  1. merge_key overlap — checks that the merge_key entries in every dataframe overlap with those in the reference (first) dataframe. If no overlap exists for any pair the function halts. If only partial overlap exists a warning is issued and only shared neighbourhoods proceed.

  2. size consistency — for neighbourhoods shared across dataframes, confirms that the size column contains identical values. Any mismatch halts the function as it indicates analyses were run on different data.

Redundant column handling:

At each pairwise merge step, columns shared between the two dataframes are compared value-by-value. Columns with identical values are dropped from the right-hand dataframe. Columns with different values are retained with _1 / _2 suffixes.

See also

nhood_diversity, nhood_cdr3_convergence, nhood_shm, nhood_annotation

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Default: merge "nhood_diversity" and "nhood_shm"
object <- merge_nhood_results(object)

# Merge three custom dataframes
object <- merge_nhood_results(
  object,
  dataframe_names = c("diversity_results", "nhood_shm", "spatial_features")
)

# Dataframes use different column names for neighbourhood size
object <- merge_nhood_results(
  object,
  dataframe_names = c("diversity_results", "nhood_shm", "spatial_features"),
  size_col = c(diversity_results = "nhood_size",
               nhood_shm         = "n_cells",
               spatial_features  = "size")
)

# Custom merge key and output name
object <- merge_nhood_results(
  object,
  dataframe_names = c("results_a", "results_b"),
  result_name     = "combined_results",
  merge_key       = "NhoodID")
} # }
